title: Renal and Cardiovascular Outcomes with Canagliflozin in Type 2 Diabetes and Nephropathy (CREDENCE)
authors: Perkovic V, Jardine MJ, Neal B, et al.
chunk_text: In patients with type 2 diabetes and kidney disease, the risk of kidney failure and cardiovascular events was significantly lower in the canagliflozin group than in the placebo group at a median follow-up of 2.62 years. Relative risk of the primary composite renal endpoint (end-stage kidney disease, doubling of serum creatinine, or renal/CV death) was reduced by 30% (HR 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59 to 0.82; P < 0.001). SGLT2 inhibition demonstrates robust renoprotection independent of glycemic control.

title: Dapagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (DAPA-CKD)
authors: Heerspink HJL, Stefánsson BV, Correa-Rotter R, et al.
chunk_text: Among patients with chronic kidney disease, regardless of the presence or absence of diabetes, the risk of a composite of a sustained decline in estimated GFR of at least 50%, end-stage kidney disease, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes was significantly lower with dapagliflozin (10 mg daily) than with placebo (HR 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.72; P < 0.001). Mortality from any cause was reduced by 31%.

title: Oral Nirmatrelvir and Ritonavir for High-Risk Non-hospitalized Patients with Covid-19 (EPIC-HR)
authors: Hammond J, Leister-Tebbe H, Gardner A, et al.
chunk_text: Treatment of symptomatic COVID-19 with oral nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir (Paxlovid) resulted in an 89% reduction in COVID-19-related hospitalization or death compared to placebo in non-hospitalized high-risk adults when initiated within 3 days of symptom onset. Ritonavir acts as a potent irreversible CYP3A4 inhibitor to boost nirmatrelvir serum levels, necessitating drug interaction screening.

title: Angiotensin-Neprilysin Inhibition versus Enalapril in Heart Failure (PARADIGM-HF)
authors: McMurray JJ, Packer M, Desai AS, et al.
chunk_text: In patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF <= 40%), sacubitril/valsartan (ARNI) was superior to enalapril in reducing the risk of death from cardiovascular causes and heart failure hospitalizations (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.73 to 0.87; P < 0.001). All-cause mortality was also significantly reduced by 16%.

title: Pembrolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Metastatic Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (KEYNOTE-189)
authors: Gandhi L, Rodríguez-Abreu D, Gadgeel S, et al.
chunk_text: Among patients with previously untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without EGFR or ALK mutations, adding pembrolizumab to standard chemotherapy with pemetrexed and platinum substantially prolonged overall survival (12-month OS rate 69.2% vs 49.4%; HR 0.49; 95% CI 0.38 to 0.64; P < 0.001) and progression-free survival across all PD-L1 expression categories.
